original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Upper bound on bounded-depth blocks of the unchanged unsigned dirty connector (PR4231/PR4248 interface): a depth-d block on k sources at characteristic c has 2^k-1 <= k*min(k,c)*binom(kc+d-2,d-1); depth-two blocks have at most log2 c + O(log log c) sources; concatenations of depth<=2 blocks have sharp leading constant 1/2 (matched by PR6071), and depth<=D concatenations are capped at (1-1/D+o(1)) c log2 c.
scope_change_reason: The alphabet stays fixed. This follows the released general-family handoff, PR6071 open question 1 (sharp leading constant of N(c)/(c log2 c)), and settles its depth-two part: it shows that the suggested search for depth-two blocks near 2 log2 c cannot succeed for large c.
bottleneck_link: Side result on recursive-interface capacity. It changes no supplier or kappa; it redirects further N(c) constructions from depth-two blocks to depth>=3 or non-block words.
stop_rule: Stop at the proved cap plus a literal-word verifier; do not start a depth-three construction search in this session.
evidence: README proof (weight identity); verify.py: exhaustive census of 39,288 small floor words with 1,031,591 identity checks, 21 rebuilt Gray blocks, exact capacity table to c=2^4096, four rejected controls. Standard library only.
author: JosieElliston (Claude Code session 40)
ai_assistance: Substantial: Anthropic Claude (Claude Code session 40) derived the proof, wrote the verifier and README; optional OpenAI Codex read-only review.

open_questions.question: Is there a depth-three block family with k ~ 2 log2 c (lower constant 2/3)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Depth<=2 concatenations are capped at constant 1/2; depth three is the cheapest route to a larger lower constant.
open_questions.first_step: Search small c (8..32) for depth-three blocks with k > 2 + 2 log2 c; by the theorem most first-read pairs must extend to a mask.

open_questions.question: Is the general constant of N(c)/(c log2 c) above 1/2, and is it 1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Fixed-depth block concatenations are capped at 1-1/D; the counting constant 1 needs unbounded depth or cross-block reads.
open_questions.first_step: Sharpen the global count using the coordinate structure of each read, not only its weight.
open_questions.blocked_by: Global counting gains nothing from the weight identity when n >= 2.

open_questions.question: What is the exact largest depth-two block at small c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cap is loose at practical c (21 against Gray 9 at c=2^8).
open_questions.first_step: Exact search at c=8..16; balanced Gray codes suggest about log2 c + log2 log2 c is reachable.
